excerpt: In G. Saminathan v. The State (2026 INSC 772, 31 July 2026), the Supreme Court quashes a cheating and criminal breach of trust case born of a failed joint development agreement, holding that dishonest intention must exist at the inception and that Sections 406 and 420 IPC cannot co-exist on the same facts.

title: Specific Performance and Delay: SC – Advocate Manish Jha
excerpt: In V.N.A.S. Chandran v. S. Venila (2026 INSC 776), the Supreme Court refuses specific performance of a 2004 sale agreement, holding that a buyer must prove continuous readiness and willingness and that a lapse of over two decades militates against the equitable relief.

title: When an Acquittal Stands: SC on Evidence – Advocate Manish Jha
excerpt: In Nirmala Bai Devidas Chavhan v. State of Maharashtra (2026 INSC 787), the Supreme Court upholds the acquittal of twenty accused, explaining when identical testimony suggests tutoring, when medical evidence displaces ocular accounts, and how investigative lapses weigh.

title: Section 498A and Live-In Relationships – Advocate Manish Jha
excerpt: In Dr Lokesh B.H. v. State of Karnataka (3 August 2026), the Supreme Court holds that Section 498A IPC extends to live-in relationships in the nature of marriage between consenting adults, while mandating strict Arnesh Kumar safeguards.

title: Accident Compensation for Child Victims – Advocate Manish Jha
excerpt: The Supreme Court enhances a paraplegic child's motor accident award to Rs. 83.38 lakh, holding that functional disability, skilled-worker notional income and the multiplier of 18 govern claims for catastrophically injured children.

title: Adultery Plea at Interim Maintenance Stage – Advocate Manish Jha
excerpt: In Himanshu Chordia v. State of Rajasthan (31 July 2026), the Supreme Court holds that a Section 125(4) CrPC plea of adultery must be examined at the interim maintenance stage where the material ex facie establishes the disqualification.

title: Evidence Against an Absconder: SC Limits – Advocate Manish Jha
excerpt: Acquitting a man convicted of a 1999 murder, the Supreme Court holds that a deposition recorded in an absconder's absence is inadmissible against him unless a formal Section 299 CrPC order was passed at the time.

title: Suspicion Is Not Reason to Believe: PMLA Freezing
excerpt: The Supreme Court has dismissed the Enforcement Directorate's challenge to a Delhi High Court judgment holding that bank accounts cannot be frozen under the PMLA on mere suspicion, without the recorded reason to believe the statute requires.

title: Reach Stacker Is Not a Motor Vehicle: MACT Limits
excerpt: A reach stacker operating inside the custom-bonded Inland Container Depot at Tughlakabad is not a motor vehicle and depot roads are not a public place, the Supreme Court has held, restoring the Delhi MACT's rejection of the claim.

title: Limits on Quashing an FIR: Supreme Court – Advocate Manish Jha
excerpt: Restoring quashed corruption FIRs in State of Karnataka v. Prabhu Shankar (30 July 2026), the Supreme Court reiterates that a High Court cannot conduct a mini-trial at the threshold: the only question is whether the FIR prima facie discloses a cognizable offence.

title: Property in a Wife's Name and Succession – Advocate Manish Jha
excerpt: In Shakuntala v. Robert Anthony (30 July 2026), the Supreme Court holds that property purchased in the names of the two wives devolved as each wife's own estate — Sections 35 and 38 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 governed, not Section 33.

title: Conviction in Appeal: Revision, Not Appeal
excerpt: The Supreme Court has held that no appeal lies under Section 374 CrPC or Section 415 BNSS where a Sessions Court reverses an acquittal and convicts an accused for the first time. The remedy is criminal revision, to be examined with greater scrutiny.

title: Annual Rise in Maintenance Upheld
excerpt: The Delhi High Court has upheld a five per cent yearly increase built into a Family Court maintenance order, holding it a lawful means of preserving the real value of the award against inflation.

title: Review of Sanction Under Section 19 PC Act
excerpt: A considered refusal of sanction to prosecute a public servant cannot be reopened on the same material. The Supreme Court declined to interfere with the quashing of a sanction granted after a reference from the Chief Minister's office, and imposed costs.

title: Parity in Bail: A Delhi High Court Order
excerpt: An order of 31 July 2026 illustrates three considerations that most often decide a regular bail application: the role attributed to the applicant, the position of co-accused already released, and the stage the trial has reached.

title: Maintenance in Delhi Family Courts
excerpt: A step by step account of how a maintenance application proceeds in the Family Courts of Delhi, from filing and the affidavit of assets through interim relief, evidence, the final order and enforcement.
